  Regular Meeting Minutes
  April 9, 2026

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Commissioner Pelayo

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Executive Assistant
Present: Chair Flores, Vice Chair Ruiz, Secretary Cynthia Esquivel and Commissioner Edgar Pelayo;
Commissioner Trujillo had an excused absence.
Staff: Acting Director of Parks & Recreation Tina De La Rosa, Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey, and
Recreation Manager James Markel.

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: Cyndi Anderson SG resident, there is a lot of misinformation regarding removal of Coach
Sifuentes from JAA. The decision had nothing to do with politics, as he was removed a week before
attending the City Council meeting. He claims he did not know how to get on the board however she has
repeatedly sent information over to him and explained the process as well. She explained the way the
board of review works and stated that Coach Sifuentes should be used to being removed as it has
happened at other cities. Voiced her displeasure with the lies and him using youth programs as a pawn.

Recognized: An email from Mario Dominguez SG resident - Due to the possible renaming of Cesar Chavez
Park, he would like the Commission to reconsider renaming Hollydale Community Park to avoid confusion
with similarly named parks. Suggested approaches include selecting a unique name such as “Wonderland
Park” or inviting community input through a public naming process and vote.

Recognized: An email from Celina Zepeda SG resident – Is requesting the Commission’s support in
opposing the six-month pool closure, as it would significantly impact the SG Aqua Coalition swim club and
the broader swimming community. The closure would reduce training opportunities, affect athletes’ ability
to qualify for competitive events, and create challenges in maintaining affordable program access for local
families.

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. POLICE DEPARTMENT ORAL SAFETY REPORT
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Vice Chair Ruiz
Acting Director De La Rosa introduced Lieutenant Gonzalez, who reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.
Vice Chair Ruiz asked if any PD can be dispatched to Urban Orchard Park to deter theft. Lt. Gonzalez thinks
that it’s a good idea, however, due to budget cuts, might not be possible. Commissioner Pelayo suggested
posting on social media or bike patrol as another option. Chair Flores asked if there will be issues due to
budget cuts; Lt. Gonzalez stated that there will be less patrol and slower response times.

Recognized: Jimmy Ozaeta SG resident, wants cannabis smoking to be addressed at SG Park as well as
illegal gambling with mobile bars out of vehicles.

 2. PARK FACILITY MAINTENANCE DIVISION ANNUAL REPORT
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Secretary Esquivel
Parks Superintendent Massey reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.

Recognized: Jimmy Ozaeta SG resident, glad to see Glenn back. Suggests that CDBG funds be used for
maintenance of the parks considering budget cuts.

Recognized: Cyndi Anderson SG resident, CDBG have been used in the past for park issues, mentioned an
incident in the past with leaking roof at Sports Center. Questioned if park received funds, a discussion
ensued. Understood that the money wasn’t lost.

Recognized: An email from Mario Dominguez SG resident – In light of the City’s current financial
challenges, he is requesting information on the costs associated with key community events including
Winter Wonderland, the Christmas parade, Breakfast with Santa, and the Rotary Thanksgiving Dinner.
Additionally, please provide the funding sources for each event, including whether they are supported by
the general fund.

3. PROPOSED PROGRAM FEES FOR FY 2026/27
Recommended Motion: Approve the Proposed Fee Schedule for May 11, 2026, to May 11, 2027
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Vice Chair Ruiz

specifically for the pool. Recreation Manager Markel went into detail addressing the commissioners.

Recognized: Nadia SG resident, discussed concerns regarding potential pool closure. Stated that there are
other programs that can be removed rather than closing the pool.

Recognized: Caroline Magana, SG resident, concerned about pool closure. Expressed displeasure at long
lines for signups. Not against raising fees to continue pool operation as there is a counterbalance in
increasing fees.

Recognized: Trinidad Maravilla, SG resident, does not agree on increasing fees as there are lower income
families with multiple children in sports who would not be able to afford them. This will result in
community members going to other cities.

4. REVIEW OF CONCESSION AGREEMENTS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Secretary Esquivel

for renewal.
Commissioner Pelayo requested copy of current concessions agreements on list be provided to the
Commission.

Recognized: An email from Mario Dominguez SG resident, stated he would like the Commission to explore
allowing street vendors, specifically those selling churros, to operate within South Gate Park. Clarification is
also requested on current policies that restrict this activity and whether adjustments can be made to
better accommodate community interest.
Acting Director De La Rosa, this comment does not pertain to the item.

 5. PROPOSED RENAMING OF CESAR CHAVEZ PARK
Recommended Motion: Motion to suggest new names for Cesar Chavez Park and submit to Council for
their review.
M/S/C: Secretary Esquivel/Vice Chair Ruiz
Acting Director De La Rosa reviewed this item, the following 5 names were suggested by the
Commissioners: Southern Street Park, Unity Park, Farmworker Unity Park, Linear Park, and South Gate
Gardens.

Recognized: An email from Mario Dominguez SG resident, stated he would like to propose considering the
renaming of Cesar Chavez Park, with one suggestion being Dolores Huerta Park to recognize her
contributions. Alternatively, the City may consider a community driven name process, allowing residents
to submit and vote on potential names.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Acting Director De La Rosa: Will present budget report to Council on 04/14. The Spring Carnival brought in
$21,000 in revenue which will be used towards 4th of July fireworks show. Easter Fest sold out with 325
tickets being sold although capacity was 300. In Youth Programming, dance recitals sold out. Sports Camp
had a lower attendance this year. Teen Programs have been great, steady numbers. Teens really enjoyed
their first trip to Knott’s Berry Farm; there are a few trips scheduled for this summer. At the Senior Center
the HSA lunch program continues to be successful. The Eco Garden event on April 4th sold out at Urban
Orchard Park again. New classes began; 7 people attended the Below Mindset Class. At Circle Park, futsal
went well, there were 5 participants. No participants for basketball or pickleball, staff is being flexible to fill
in. Upcoming events: Earth Day, Alma Querida Dear Soul art exhibit and Miss South Gate Pageant on April
18th. Grand opening of Soccer USA fields on 04/16. Auditorium roofing project completed, Office A staff
back in the office.

Recreation Manager Markel: Contract for Swim Stadium electronic scoreboard project awarded and is in
procurement. Items will be delivered by end of May or early June, with installation scheduled for mid-June
and completion by June 30th. Swim Stadium project is 100% paid for by CDBG funding. Shade structure
project takes longer to procure. Initially thought it would take 3-6 months to complete however will likely
take 8-12 months as customized structures are needed. Funding not lost on this project.

Parks Supt. Massey: Resurfacing of Tot Lot at Hollydale Regional Park to begin next week and will take
about a month to complete. Funded by CDBG funding.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Vice Chair Ruiz: Thankful for the renovation of the Tot Lot. Asked if they can commit to the Carnival for
future revenue and if they can pay for security as well.

Commissioner Pelayo: Asked about the Carnival cost structure and whether it was profitable. Encouraged
acting Dir. De La Rosa and Sup. Massey to attend the advisory committee to potentially get additional
CDBG funds.

contracts. He also requested that the Commissioners be copied in when responding to Mr. Dominguez’
email. Vice Chair Ruiz requested how the park is providing better safety for runners.

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

The Parks and Recreation Commission will receive a refresher from the City Attorney
on key governance and procedural requirements. The presentation will include a review
of Robert’s Rules of Order as a framework for conducting meetings in an orderly, fair,
and efficient manner. Topics will include making and seconding motions, maintaining
decorum, and following established procedures to support clear and effective decision-
making. In addition, the City Attorney will provide an overview of the Brown Act,
emphasizing requirements for transparency, public participation, and open decision-
making. Commissioners will be reminded of their responsibilities to ensure compliance.

The presentation will also outline the roles and responsibilities of Parks and Recreation
Commissioners, highlighting their advisory function, ethical obligations, and the
importance of representing community interests while supporting City policies and
goals.

To provide  world  class  youth  soccer  programs  that  enrich  children's  lives.

AYSO  Mission  Statement
American  Youth  Soccer  Organization's  mission  is to develop  quality  youth  soccer  programs  which  promote  a fun,
family  environment  based  on the following  AYSO  philosophies...

AYSO  Philosophies

Eveiyone  Plays@
Our program's goal is for kids to play soccer so we mandate that every player on every team must
play at least 50% of every game. It's no fun to spend the game on the bench...and  that's no way to
learn soccer!

Balanced Teams
Each year we Form new teams as evenly balanced as possible because it's more fun and a better
learning experience  when teams of similar ability play. It allows for each player to gain the experience
of a wide variety of teammates  of different skill levels.

Open Registration
Our program is open to all children between 4 and 19 years of age who want to register and play
soccer. Interest and enthusiasm  are the only criteria for playing. There are no elimination try-outs and
nobody gets cut.

Positive Coaching
Encouragement  of player effort provides for greater enjoyment for the players and leads to better-
skilled and better-motivated  players. A coach can be one of the most influential people in a child's  life,
so AYSO requires they create a positive experience  for every boy and girl.

Good Spommanship
We strive to create a positive environment  based on mutual respect rather than a win-at-all-costs
attitude, and our program is designed to instill good sportsmanship in every facet of AYSO.

Player Development
We believe that all players should be able to develop their soccer skills and knowledge to the best of
their abilities, both individually and as members of a team, in order to maximize their enjoyment of the
game.

The Aquatics Division maintained steady operations throughout the third quarter, with a

competitive aquatics.

The Swim Stadium continued to operate seven days a week year-round, offering a
variety of Adult, Lap, and Family Swim sessions. Recreational swim attendance
exceeded 5,000 visits this quarter, including more than 4,000 member scan-ins and
nearly 1,000 daily admissions. Membership levels remained strong, with over 3,000
active accounts, primarily consisting of Adult and Senior Splash memberships.

Aquatic fitness classes continued through the winter months. Staff offered over 72 hours
of aquatic fitness and therapy opportunities. SeniorCise, Aqua Blast, Aqua Aerobics,
and Master Swim remained popular, with Staff actively diversifying class offerings in
preparation for increased spring participation.

Aquatics partnerships and competitive programming continued to be a central
component of facility operations. The Swim Stadium remained home to three local,
competitive swim teams: South Gate Aqua Coalition (SGAC), Lynwood Marlins Swim
Team (LMST), and Penguins Aquatic Club (PAC). Collectively, these teams brought
approximately 120 youth swimmers to the facility daily through consistent weekly
practices. The Swim Stadium also served as a regional competition venue, hosting
several large-scale events. In January, the facility hosted a South-Central Swim League
meet that drew nearly 500 athletes and their families. In February, the South-Central

approximately 200 combined private and semi-private enrollments. As in previous
quarters, youth participants between the ages of 6 and 17 make up the majority of

safety education.
